summary: Intermittent gRPC channel drops due to edge proxy idle-close causing serving node KV-cache coherence and high tail latency
description: Customer reports intermittent 5xxs and long tail latency for streaming responses from their Private deployment. Errors correlate with long-lived sessions; behavior started after a corporate edge proxy change on the customer side. Initial hypothesis is that the corporate edge/proxy closes idle TCP connections (60s) which causes gRPC streams to drop and the serving runtime to re-establish sessions in a way that temporarily breaks KV cache coherence, producing downstream cache cold-starts and 5xx errors.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private stack with the customer's edge proxy enabled in path (proxy configured with default idle timeout ~60s).
2) Start a long-lived streaming chat session to the hosted model and leave it idle for ~70s,
3) Resume the stream and observe either a client-side gRPC error (CANCELLED/UNAVAILABLE) or higher tail latency on the resumed request,
4) Observe serving node logs for stream reconnect and KV cache eviction/rehydration events.
logs: tcpdump sample: repeated FIN packets from customer-proxy at ~60s idle; gRPC client sees UNAVAILABLE then reconnect. Serving-runtime logs show 'session closed: EOF' followed by 'kv-cache-miss: prefetch-trigger' and a spike in token generation latency. Examples attached in Confluence runbook link.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Support triaged with customer; customer provided tcpdumps and proxy config showing idle-timeout=60s.
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE reproduced on staging by inserting an HTTP edge that closes idle TCP at 60s; observed identical client disconnect and streaming reinit sequence.

Network capture: client TCP FIN initiated by proxy, server sends FIN-ACK; gRPC connection is not transitioning cleanly to keepalive-based probe - re-establish causes serving-runtime to spin up a new session and reload KV cache state for that model shard.
Serving runtime metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate drops from 98% to 12% on reconnect; token_latency_p95 jumps from 120ms to 1.8s for first few requests after reconnect.

Hypothesis: edge idle-close prevents gRPC keepalive probes from keeping connection alive. The runtime assumes long-lived channels and uses in-memory KV cache warm state tied to a connection lifecycle; abrupt close causes a short window where prefetch/replica warmup hasn't completed, leading to request timeouts and transient 503/504s.
Validated that customer ALB/proxy change coincided with incident start time (change approved 2026-03-09).
SRE reproduced workaround by setting keepalive and lowering KV prefetch dependency; successful mitigation observed.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-10: Collected tcpdump and proxy config from customer. Ticket created and triaged as P1 due to customer-facing errors.
Benji Morales (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging using a proxy that enforces 60s idle-close. Confirming impact on kv-cache warmup. Working on short-term mitigation and long-term fix.
Customer (Pinebrook Health) 2026-03-10: We rolled a proxy policy last week; happy to revert but need guidance on safe values for production.

Benji Morales 2026-03-11: Short-term mitigation tested: 1) Increase customer proxy idle timeout to >=300s OR enable TCP keepalive/HTTP/2 ping support; 2) Runtime patch to tolerate GOAWAY/FIN and trigger faster warmup with reduced tail latency (PR linked).
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12: Customer applied idle-timeout=360s in staging; errors stopped. Customer agreed to a staged production change after a maintenance window.
Benji Morales 2026-03-12: Created follow-up task to remove KV-cache connection affinity and add robust reconnect warmup (longer-term fix).
resolution: Workaround validated and applied: customer increased edge-proxy idle timeout to 360s and enabled gRPC keepalive. This eliminated the immediate disconnects and restored normal kv_cache hit rates. Engineering merged a serving-runtime patch to make KV-cache rehydration asynchronous and resilient to short reconnects (see PR). Planned follow-up: runtime release 0.43.2 with improved warmup + docs for recommended proxy settings for Private deployments.
postmortem_follow_up: Create a KB article for customer-run proxy tuning (idle-timeout >= 300s or gRPC ping/keepalive enabled); add a config flag in private-deploy that validates edge/proxy settings on bootstrap; schedule runtime patch rollout in 0.43.2.
notes_for_sales_customer_success: Pinebrook Health is Private-tier with sensitive workloads. Recommend coordinating change window and provide engineering support during production idle-timeout update. Offer a free 4-hour SRE engagement to implement recommended proxy tuning and validate after cutover.
